slice_subject: The AI Scientist-v2 as evidence for end-to-end scientist-agent capability and its present verification ceiling

primary_sources.title: The AI Scientist-v2: Workshop-Level Automated Scientific Discovery via Agentic Tree Search
The AI Scientist Generates its First Peer-Reviewed Scientific Publication

observations: The technical report describes an end-to-end agentic system that formulates hypotheses, designs and executes experiments, analyzes and visualizes results, and writes manuscripts.
The v2 system replaces the predecessor's reliance on human-authored code templates and uses progressive agentic tree search coordinated by an experiment-manager agent.
Three fully autonomous manuscripts were submitted to an ICLR workshop and one passed the workshop peer-review threshold.

The project team's own report states that none of the three manuscripts, as submitted, met what the team regarded as ICLR main-conference standards and explicitly documents failure modes including citation mistakes and other manuscript-quality issues.
inference: This is direct evidence that a scientist-agent architecture can close a substantial research loop without per-project human code templates, but the strongest supported claim is workshop-level autonomous ML research under a bounded evaluation setting. The same primary evidence argues against treating paper acceptance as sufficient proof of reliable scientific correctness. For Phase-1 scientist-agent design, independent verification, reproducibility checks, and evidence-grounded citation/claim validation remain first-class bottlenecks rather than post-processing details.
uncertainty: The acceptance result is one accepted workshop paper from three autonomous submissions and should not be generalized to broad scientific domains or main-conference-quality research.
The audit did not independently rerun the generated experiments in this bounded slice.
No claim is made here that autonomous scientist agents have achieved general scientific reliability.
continuation: Next scientist_agents invocation: audit one independent primary-source evaluation or replication of an autonomous scientist system, focusing specifically on correctness/reproducibility evidence and failure detection; do not read other workers or downstream outputs as exploration direction, and keep the next run to one bounded leaf.
